identity.title: WebGen-Bench: Evaluating LLMs on Generating Interactive and Functional Websites from Scratch

problem.claim: Measure how well LLM-based agents create functional, interactive, multi-file websites from scratch.

contributions.claim: Introduces WebGen-Bench, covering three major and thirteen minor web-application categories with 647 manually refined functional test cases.
Constructs WebGen-Instruct, a dataset of 6,667 website-generation instructions, and releases datasets, code, and model weights.
Reports evaluations of Bolt.diy, OpenHands, and Aider with proprietary and open-source LLM engines, plus training of Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct on Bolt.diy trajectories.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe WebGen-Bench as a novel benchmark for measuring from-scratch multi-file website generation by LLM-based agents.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that Bolt.diy powered by DeepSeek-R1 achieves 27.8% accuracy on the benchmark test cases.
The authors report that training Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct on trajectories from a subset of WebGen-Instruct reaches 38.2% accuracy, exceeding the best proprietary model's reported performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLM-based agents are positioned as promising for code generation and management in complex codebases.
WebGen-Bench measures from-scratch multi-file website creation using diverse human- and GPT-4o-assisted instructions across web-application categories.
Functionality-specific operations and expected outcomes define 647 manually refined test cases, executed by a web-navigation agent.
Three code-agent frameworks are evaluated; the reported best baseline reaches 27.8%, while trajectory training with WebGen-Instruct is reported at 38.2%.

source_observation.claim: The benchmark operationalizes website quality as agreement between observed and expected outcomes for specified operations, using an automated web-navigation agent.

lessons.interpretation: Function-level behavioral checks can make broad generation tasks more concrete and comparable.
lessons.application: For an interactive-generation study, define per-instruction operations and expected outcomes before evaluation, then report aggregate behavioral accuracy.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when quality depends mainly on aesthetics, maintainability, or open-ended user experience rather than testable behavior.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the category distribution, test-case weighting, execution environment, or aggregation details behind the accuracy scores.
The subset and training procedure for the 38.2% result, and the identity and score of the best proprietary model, are not detailed.
No ablations or uncertainty estimates are reported in the abstract.
